items.title: How Uyghurs from China helped Syrian rebels overthrow Bashar al-Assad
items.description: Motivated to avenge their families in China, Uyghur mercenaries became valued fighting partners for Syria's rebels. Their participation helped Syria's new president ultimately win Syria's civil war.

items.title: Leaders eye on Belarus for signs it might offer Russia help in Ukraine
items.description: Belarus’ exiled opposition leader visits Kyiv as the city recovers from Russia’s largest missile attack of the year. World leaders are closely watching Belarus’ potential support for Russia’s invasion.

items.title: Everything We Know About the Deadly Ukrainian Strike in Occupied Luhansk
items.description: Russia said at least 21 people were killed in the overnight strike on a college dormitory, while Ukraine denied targeting civilians.

items.title: France and Mali's pro-independence rebels: A history shaped by alliances and mutual interests
items.description: Bamako's military junta has accused Paris of supporting the Azawad Liberation Front (ALF), which launched an offensive in northern Mali at the end of April. These claims are based on the French authorities' historical ties with the pro-independence rebel groups, though those connections have since weakened.

items.title: Massive Russian strike on Kyiv: ‘I hope my friends are alive’
items.description: The overnight Russian attack on Ukraine, which centred on the capital, Kyiv, reportedly involved some 90 missiles, including a powerful hypersonic ballistic missile and 60 drones. The senior UN official in the country called for an end to civilian harm.

items.title: Rosenberg: Luhansk strike sparks Russian accusations and vow to retaliate
items.description: Eighteen people were killed and 42 others injured in the strike on the town in Russian-occupied eastern Ukraine.

items.title: Serbia: Police clash with protesters urging early elections
items.description: Officers fired teargas and stun grenades as tens of thousands rallied against President Aleksandar Vucic's government. The demonstration went ahead despite the state rail operator canceling trains to and from Belgrade.
